name: Deepwell Den — The Floating Card Game
description: Deepwell Den is a legendary floating card game that has operated continuously since 2193, rotating through a circuit of basements, barge interiors, and decommissioned hab blocks across the Shelf and lower Tier 2 districts on a schedule communicated only through word of mouth and trusted intermediaries. The game runs a modified form of neural poker where BCI bluff-detection is blocked by a proprietary signal-dampening rig — the only version of the game where raw human psychological skill still determines outcomes. Stakes range from Φ20 to tables where a single hand can turn Φ15,000, and the Den's reputation for scrupulous fairness has made it a neutral ground where Shelf factions, runners, bookmakers, and occasionally Tier 3 downward-mobile professionals sit at the same table.
story_hooks: A character is invited to Deepwell Den by someone who owes them a favor — but the invitation is actually a setup, and the table they're joining has a very specific reason for wanting them present.
The Den's signal-dampening rig has gone missing between locations, and without it the game loses its entire identity — finding it means navigating the Shelf's full social web.
A regular Den player has been winning at a rate that should be impossible without BCI advantage, and no one can figure out how they're doing it.
